findings.title: Substring match for error-focused query misclassifies negated queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` determines whether a discover query is error-focused by checking if the literal substring "event.type:error" appears anywhere in the lowercased query string. This naive check does not account for negation: a query like `!event.type:error` (which explicitly excludes error events) contains the substring "event.type:error" and will be incorrectly classified as error-focused. As a result, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` will return True and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` will rewrite `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count` (a `sum(sample_weight)` aggregation) for a query that is explicitly NOT about errors, producing wrong/garbage counts (or query errors if `sample_weight` is absent for non-error rows) for any caller using negated error filters.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined with a docstring stating it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency", but no caller of this function exists anywhere in the diff or referenced code (no signal handler, no option-update hook). The only real mitigation against a stale allowlist decision is the 60-second TTL in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. This means that when a project is removed from (or added to) the allowlist, the previous eligibility decision can continue to be served for up to 60 seconds with no mechanism to force a refresh, contradicting the documented intent of the invalidation helper and leaving dead code that gives a false sense of correctness.

findings.title: Unrelated nested repository/submodule reference added
findings.body: This PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing a git submodule-style reference ("Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a") pointing back to the base commit of this very repository. This is unrelated to the error-upsampling feature described in the PR and looks like an accidental artifact (e.g., a nested git clone or submodule added by mistake). It should be removed before merge since it can confuse git tooling, bloat the repository, or break CI checkout steps that don't expect a submodule here.

findings.title: No tests for the public caching entry point or cache invalidation helper
findings.body: The test file exercises the private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, but never tests the actual public function `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, which contains the new caching logic (cache hit/miss paths, TTL, and the AND-combination with `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`). `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is also completely untested. Since the caching behavior is the core 'performance optimization' being introduced by this PR, and is the most likely place for subtle bugs (e.g., stale cache across allowlist changes), this is a significant gap in test coverage.

findings.title: Unrelated user-facing error message text changed in an upsampling PR
findings.body: The validation error message for `topEvents <= 0` was changed from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1". This wording change is unrelated to the error-upsampling feature this PR claims to implement, is not covered by any added/updated test asserting the new message, and silently changes an API error response that external clients or existing tests might depend on verbatim.

findings.title: Column transformation only matches an exact 'count()' string, missing aliased/equation variants
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites a column when, after lowering and stripping, it equals exactly `"count()"`. Any variant such as an already-aliased column (`"count() as total"`), an equation wrapping count (`"equation|count() / 2"`), or extra internal whitespace (`"count( )"`) will not match and will silently fall through unmodified, meaning the upsampling transform silently fails to apply for these forms while the caller believes upsampling is enabled. This can produce inconsistent results between different query shapes (e.g., top-events queries that generate aliased column strings) without any error or log indicating the transform was skipped.

findings.title: upsampled_count() assumes sample_weight is populated for all events, risking undercounting
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function computes `toInt64(sum(Column("sample_weight")))` and is used as a drop-in replacement for `count()` whenever upsampling is enabled for a project. If `sample_weight` is NULL/absent for any error events that predate this feature or were ingested without the `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` field (i.e., normal, non-client-sampled errors), ClickHouse's `sum()` will not count those rows as 1 (as plain `count()` would), but will effectively contribute 0, causing the upsampled count to be lower than the true event count for projects/time ranges with mixed sampled and non-sampled events. The code comments explicitly assume 'the database schema ensures sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects' without any validation or test covering historical/non-sampled events, making this a real data-correctness risk if that assumption doesn't hold.
